rubrics.title: Analytical Thinking
criteria: Separates facts, assumptions and unknowns
Uses evidence proportionate to the decision
Identifies root causes rather than symptoms
States uncertainty and how it affects the conclusion

levels.1: Identifies obvious facts and asks for missing information when prompted.
levels.2: Structures problems independently; distinguishes evidence quality; challenges weak data.
levels.3: Guides others' analysis; spots flawed reasoning in team work quickly.
levels.4: Integrates analysis across domains; identifies systemic patterns and common causes.
levels.5: Frames enterprise questions; knows when more analysis will not change the decision.
levels.6: Shapes the questions the board asks; balances rigour with timeliness under pressure.

rubrics.title: Risk and Controls
criteria: Writes complete cause-event-consequence statements
Rates likelihood and impact consistently with scales
Assesses control design and operation separately
Prioritises by residual exposure and appetite

levels.1: Classifies risks and controls correctly with guidance.
levels.2: Maintains registers accurately; rates consistently; tracks actions.
levels.3: Designs proportionate controls; assigns ownership; reviews team assessments.
levels.4: Sets assessment standards; aggregates across domains.
levels.5: Aligns control investment with appetite and strategy.
levels.6: Owns the enterprise control philosophy and assurance model.

rubrics.title: Financial and Quantitative Modelling
criteria: Calculates expected loss and cost-benefit correctly
States assumptions, units and uncertainty
Distinguishes expected from worst-case loss
Chooses methods proportionate to the decision

levels.2: Builds simple scenario and sensitivity models.
levels.3: Uses simulation appropriately and explains limitations.
levels.4: Evaluates investments and aggregate exposure with risk-adjusted metrics.
levels.6: Sets stress-testing strategy and challenges enterprise financial plans.

rubrics.title: Communication and Influence
criteria: Leads with the message and the decision needed
Adapts to the audience's priorities and style
Escalates proportionately and on time
Maintains trust while challenging

levels.2: Presents findings to operational managers persuasively.
levels.3: Handles disagreement and negotiates action plans.
levels.6: Communicates uncertainty to boards and external stakeholders credibly.

rubrics.title: Leadership and Strategy
criteria: Acts with integrity under pressure
Develops people and allocates work fairly
Connects risk to strategic objectives
Takes accountability for decisions

levels.2: Takes ownership of assigned work and raises concerns.
levels.3: Leads a team; coaches and delegates effectively.
levels.4: Leads a function; shapes priorities across departments.
levels.5: Builds the risk strategy and culture.
levels.6: Balances growth, resilience and accountability at enterprise level.

rubrics.title: Ethical Judgement
criteria: Recognises conflicts of interest and pressure
Protects the integrity of risk information
Considers people affected by decisions
Escalates misconduct appropriately

levels.3: Supports team members who raise concerns.
levels.4: Challenges senior leaders on ethical grounds.
levels.6: Models integrity for the whole organisation.

technical: Review cards: control types, inherent vs residual
Use the Risk Assessment Workbench on three register risks
evidence: Open every key document before deciding (Investigation workspace)
analysis: Replay 'Five Whys at the Loading Dock'
Practise scenario analysis in the Financial Lab
Review cards: root cause, concentration risk
prioritization: Rank register risks against appetite in the Workbench
Run a crisis exercise focusing on the most severe threat first
financial: Run Monte Carlo and cost-benefit in the Financial Lab
decision: Record confidence before decisions to build calibration
Read the luck-versus-judgement notes in debriefs
Review card: decision quality versus outcome
communication: Replay a write-up step and compare with the model answer
Reply to inbox messages using the stakeholder's preferred style
stakeholder: Study stakeholder preferences in the Stakeholder screen
ethics: Review cards: independence and conflicts, tolerance
Consider who bears the consequences in each option
leadership: Run a crisis exercise as incident lead
strategy: Generate a board risk summary and critique it

scoring_notes: Competency scores move towards demonstrated performance using an adaptive moving average. Worked examples reduce the weight of evidence. Promotion requires minimum scores, not just XP.
